p.src: Now the Great Sage Equal to Heaven was, after all, a demon monkey. He knew nothing of official rank or grade, nor did he compare the size of stipends; he was content merely to have his name entered on the rolls. The immortal clerks of the two bureaus attached to the Residence of Equaling Heaven attended him morning and evening. He did nothing but eat three meals by day and sleep on one couch by night; with no business to trouble him, he was perfectly free and at ease. In his leisure he visited friends in their palaces, made new companions, and swore brotherhood with them. When he met the Three Pure Ones, he addressed them as “Venerable”; when he encountered the Four Emperors, he called them “Your Majesty.” As for the Nine Luminaries, the Generals of the Five Regions, the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions, the Four Heavenly Kings, the Twelve Chronological Spirits, the Five Elders of the Five Regions, all the constellations of heaven, and the host of gods of the Milky Way, he treated and addressed every one of them simply as a brother. Today he wandered east, tomorrow he roamed west; coming and going on the clouds, he never stayed in one place.

p.src: One day, during the Jade Emperor’s morning court, the Perfected Immortal Xu Jingyang stepped out from the assembled ranks, bowed his head, and memorialized: “At present the Great Sage Equal to Heaven has no duties and spends his time idly roaming about. He befriends all the constellations of heaven and, regardless of their rank, calls them all his companions. I fear that with so much leisure he may eventually cause trouble. It would be better to put some duty in his charge, so that no other trouble may arise.” On hearing this, the Jade Emperor immediately issued a summons. The Monkey King came delightedly and said, “Your Majesty, what promotion or reward have you summoned old Monkey to receive?” The Jade Emperor said, “Seeing that you are idle and without occupation, We shall give you a duty. For the time being, take charge of the Peach Garden of Immortality, and attend to it carefully day and night.” The Great Sage joyfully gave thanks for the imperial favor, made his obeisance before the throne, and withdrew.

The local tutelary god of the garden stopped him and asked, “Where are you going, Great Sage?” The Great Sage replied, “I have been appointed by the Jade Emperor to take charge of the Peach Garden in his stead, and have come now to inspect it.” The local god hurriedly saluted, then called over the whole company of mighty workers who hoed the trees, carried water, tended the peaches, and swept the grounds. They all came to kowtow before the Great Sage and escorted him inside. There he beheld:

p.src: After admiring and enjoying the sights for a long while, the Great Sage asked the local god, “How many trees are there?” The local god replied, “There are three thousand six hundred trees. The first twelve hundred bear sparse blossoms and small fruit, ripening once every three thousand years. Whoever eats them becomes an immortal and attains the Way, with a strong body made light. The middle twelve hundred have layered blossoms and sweet fruit, ripening once every six thousand years. Whoever eats them rises aloft on rosy clouds and enjoys eternal youth and life. The rear twelve hundred have purple-veined fruit with pale-yellow kernels, ripening once every nine thousand years. Whoever eats them lives as long as Heaven and Earth and is as ancient as the sun and moon.” The Great Sage was overjoyed at these words. That day he finished counting the trees, inspected the pavilions, and returned to his residence. From then on, he came to admire the garden once every few days and ceased visiting friends or roaming elsewhere.

p.src: One day he saw that most of the peaches on the old trees had ripened. He longed to taste a fresh one, but the garden’s local god and mighty workers, together with the immortal clerks of the Residence of Equaling Heaven, followed him so closely that he had no chance. Suddenly he devised a plan and said, “Wait outside the gate for now, and let me rest a while in this pavilion.” All the immortals duly withdrew. The Monkey King then removed his cap and official robe, climbed a great tree, chose the fully ripened peaches, and plucked a great many, feasting at his ease among the branches. When he had eaten his fill, he leapt down from the tree, put on his cap and robe, summoned his attendants, and returned ceremoniously to his residence. Two or three days later, he went back and contrived to steal more peaches, indulging himself to his heart’s content.

p.src: One day, the Queen Mother prepared a banquet, opened wide the jeweled pavilions, and arranged a grand Festival of Immortal Peaches at the Jasper Pool. She ordered the seven immortal maidens—clad in red, blue, white, black, purple, yellow, and green—to carry flower baskets on their heads to the Peach Garden and gather fruit for the feast. When the seven maidens reached the garden gate, they found the local god and mighty workers of the Peach Garden, together with the immortal clerks of the two bureaus of the Residence of Equaling Heaven, all guarding the entrance. The maidens stepped forward and said, “By the Queen Mother’s gracious command, we have come to gather peaches for the banquet.” The local god said, “Immortal maidens, please wait. This year is different from former years. The Jade Emperor has appointed the Great Sage Equal to Heaven to supervise this place. We must inform the Great Sage before we dare open the garden.” The maidens asked, “Where is the Great Sage?” The local god replied, “The Great Sage is inside the garden. Feeling weary, he is sleeping by himself in the pavilion.” The maidens said, “If so, let us go and find him. We must not delay.” The local god immediately went in with them. They searched as far as the flower pavilion but did not find him. Only his cap and robe lay there; no one knew where he had gone, and they could find him nowhere in the vicinity. In fact, after amusing himself and eating several peaches, the Great Sage had transformed into a tiny man two inches tall and fallen asleep beneath the thick leaves at the top of a great tree. The seven maidens said, “We came here by imperial command. If we cannot find the Great Sage, how dare we return empty-handed?” An immortal attendant nearby said, “Since you maidens have come by command, there is no need to hesitate. Our Great Sage is accustomed to wandering at leisure. I expect he has left the garden to visit friends. Go ahead and gather the peaches; we will answer to him on your behalf.”

p.src: Following his advice, the maidens entered the grove to gather peaches. They first filled two baskets from the front trees, then three baskets from the middle trees. But when they came to gather fruit from the rear trees, they found the blossoms and fruit sparse, with only a few downy-stemmed, green-skinned peaches remaining. The truth was that the Monkey King had eaten all the ripe ones. The seven immortal maidens looked all around and saw only one peach, half red and half white, on a branch facing south. The maiden in blue pulled the branch down by hand, and the maiden in red plucked the peach; then they let the branch spring upward again.

p.src: As it happened, the Great Sage, in his transformed shape, had been sleeping on that very branch, and they woke him with a start. The Great Sage instantly resumed his true form, drew the golden-hooped staff from his ear, and gave it a shake until it became as thick as a rice bowl. With a fierce shout he cried, “What manner of monsters are you, that you dare steal my peaches?” The seven immortal maidens were so frightened that they all knelt together and said, “Great Sage, calm your anger. We are not monsters, but the seven robed immortal maidens sent by the Queen Mother to gather immortal peaches for the grand banquet in the jeweled pavilions. When we arrived, we first met the local god of the garden and the other divinities, but though we searched for the Great Sage, we could not find you. Fearing that we might delay the Queen Mother’s gracious command, we could not wait for the Great Sage and therefore began gathering peaches first. We earnestly beg you to forgive us.” On hearing this, the Great Sage’s anger turned to delight, and he said, “Immortal maidens, please rise. Whom has the Queen Mother invited to the banquet in her pavilions?” A maiden replied, “The previous gatherings followed an established custom. The guests were the venerable Buddhas of the Western Heaven, bodhisattvas, holy monks, and arhats; Guanyin of the Southern Pole in the south; the Holy Emperor of Sublime Grace and the immortal elders of the Ten Continents and Three Isles in the east; the Mystic Spirit of the Northern Pole in the north; and the Great Immortal Yellow Horn of the Yellow Pole in the center. These are the Five Elders of the Five Regions. There are also the Star Lords of the Five Bushels; from the upper eight grottoes, the Three Pure Ones, the Four Emperors, the Taiyi celestial immortals, and their company; from the middle eight grottoes, the Jade Emperor, the immortals of the Nine Mounds, seas, and mountains; and from the lower eight grottoes, the Lord of the Underworld and the terrestrial immortals who dwell among mankind. All the great and lesser honored gods of every palace and hall attend the splendid Festival of Immortal Peaches together.” The Great Sage laughed and asked, “Have I been invited?” The maiden replied, “We have heard nothing of it.” The Great Sage said, “I am the Great Sage Equal to Heaven. Why should old Monkey not be invited as an honored guest at the head of the feast?” The maiden said, “Those were the old rules for earlier gatherings. We do not know what arrangements have been made for this one.” The Great Sage said, “That is true enough; you are not to blame. Stand here for the moment while old Monkey goes first to learn the news and see whether or not I have been invited.”

p.src: The Barefoot Immortal came face-to-face with the Great Sage. The Great Sage lowered his head and devised a scheme to deceive the true immortal, so that he himself might secretly attend the banquet. He asked, “Where are you going, venerable Daoist?” The immortal replied, “The Queen Mother has summoned me to attend the Grand Festival of Immortal Peaches.” The Great Sage said, “Then you have not heard. Because my somersault cloud is swift, the Jade Emperor ordered me to invite all the worthies along five routes. You are first to rehearse the ceremonial courtesies at the Hall of Brightness, and only afterward proceed to the banquet.” The immortal was an upright and honorable man, so he took the lie for truth and said, “In former years we always rehearsed the rites and gave thanks at the Jasper Pool. Why must we now perform them first at the Hall of Brightness before attending the festival at the Jasper Pool?” Having no choice, he turned his auspicious cloud around and went straight to the Hall of Brightness.

p.src: The Great Sage could not take in all the sights when suddenly the fragrance of wine assailed his nostrils. Turning his head, he saw beneath a long gallery on the right several immortal officials who brewed the wine and mighty attendants who strained the lees, together with Daoist servants who carried water and boys who tended the fires. They were washing vats and scrubbing jars, having already made nectareous liquor, ambrosial wine, fragrant ales, and choice brews. The Great Sage could not keep the saliva from running at the corners of his mouth and wanted a drink, but all those people were still there. So he worked a spell: he plucked several hairs from his body, put them into his mouth and chewed them to pieces, then spat them out, recited an incantation, and cried, “Change!” They instantly changed into several sleep-inducing insects and flew at the faces of the workers. Just look at them: their hands went limp, their heads drooped, and their eyes closed. Dropping their implements, they all nodded off. The Great Sage took some delicacies of a hundred flavors, rare viands, and exotic dishes into the gallery. There, beside the vats and close to the jars, he cast restraint aside and drank his fill. After feasting for a long while, he became dead drunk. Then, feeling and fumbling about himself, he thought, “This is bad, bad! When the invited guests arrive in a little while, will they not blame me? If they seize me on the spot, what shall I do? I had better return early to my residence and sleep it off.”

p.src: The Great Sage staggered and swayed, emboldened by wine, blundering wherever he pleased. Presently he took the wrong road and arrived not at the Residence of the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, but at the Tushita Palace. The sight of it suddenly brought him to his senses. “The Tushita Palace stands above the Thirty-three Heavens, in the Heaven Beyond Grief, and is the dwelling of the Most High Lord Lao. How did I stray here? Well, well! I have long wished to visit the old gentleman but never found the chance. Since my faltering steps have brought me here today, I may as well pay him a call.” He straightened his clothes and barged inside, but Lord Lao was nowhere to be seen, and not a soul was about. As it happened, Lord Lao was expounding the Way with the Ancient Buddha Dipankara upon the Vermilion Mound Cinnabar Terrace in the three-storied tower, while all the immortal boys, generals, officials, and attendants stood around listening. The Great Sage went straight into the alchemy chamber, but his search proved fruitless. He saw only that a fire was burning in the furnace beside the alchemical stove. Five gourds had been placed around the furnace, all filled with refined golden elixir pills. The Great Sage rejoiced. “These are the supreme treasures of the immortals. Since attaining the Way, I have understood the principle that inner and outer are alike. I too have wished to refine some golden elixir to aid others, but once I returned home I never had the leisure. By good fortune I have come upon them today. While the old fellow is away, let me eat a few and sample the new batch.” He emptied all the gourds and ate every pill, just as though he were munching roasted beans.

p.src: In a little while, the elixir filled his body and the wine wore off. He considered matters again and said to himself, “This is bad, bad! This calamity is greater than heaven itself. If the Jade Emperor learns of it, my life will be forfeit. Go, go, go! I had better descend to the lower world and be a king again.” He ran out of the Tushita Palace, avoided his former route, and escaped through the Western Gate of Heaven under a spell of invisibility. Lowering his cloud, he soon returned to the domain of the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. There he saw banners flashing and spears and halberds gleaming: the four valiant commanders and the demon kings of the seventy-two caves were drilling at arms. The Great Sage called loudly, “Little ones, I am back!” The demons dropped their weapons, knelt, and said, “How carefree you are, Great Sage! You abandoned us for so long and never came to look after us.” The Great Sage replied, “It has not been long, not long at all.”

p.src: Talking as they walked, they went straight into the depths of the cave-dwelling. The four valiant commanders swept the place and settled him in. After kowtowing in homage, they all asked, “What office did you actually hold during those hundred-odd years in Heaven, Great Sage?” The Great Sage laughed. “I remember it as scarcely half a year. How can you speak of a hundred-odd years?” A commander replied, “One day in Heaven is a year here below.” The Great Sage said, “Happily, this time the Jade Emperor showed me favor. He truly appointed me Great Sage Equal to Heaven, built me a Residence of the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, and established the two offices of Tranquility and Serene Spirit, staffed with immortal clerks and guards. Later, seeing that I had nothing to do, he ordered me to supervise the Immortal Peach Garden. Recently the Queen Mother arranged the Grand Festival of Immortal Peaches but did not invite me. Without waiting for her invitation, I went to the Jasper Pool first and stole and ate all her immortal delicacies and drank her immortal wine. I staggered out of the Jasper Pool and blundered into Lord Lao’s palace, where I also stole and ate the golden elixir from his five gourds. Fearing only that the Jade Emperor would condemn me, I have just fled through the Gate of Heaven.”

p.src: The demons were overjoyed when they heard this. They immediately prepared wine and fruit to welcome him home, filled a great stone bowl with coconut wine, and offered it to him. The Great Sage took one sip, bared his teeth, twisted his mouth, and said, “It tastes bad, it tastes bad.” Commanders Beng and Ba said, “Having eaten immortal wine and celestial delicacies in the heavenly palace, Great Sage, you naturally find coconut wine less pleasing to the palate. As the saying goes, ‘Fair or foul, the water of home is best.’” The Great Sage said, “And you are, as they say, ‘Kin or no kin, the folk of home are dearest.’ While enjoying myself at the Jasper Pool this morning, I saw many bottles and jars beneath the long gallery, all filled with nectareous and ambrosial wine. None of you has ever tasted it. Wait here while I go back and steal several bottles. If each of you drinks half a cup, every one of you will gain immortality.” The monkeys were beside themselves with joy.

p.src: Now the seven fairy maidens, having been immobilized by the Great Sage's spell, were not released until a full celestial day had passed. Each took up her flower basket and returned to report to the Queen Mother, saying, “The Great Sage Equal to Heaven used magic to hold us fast, and that is why we are late.” The Queen Mother asked, “How many immortal peaches did you gather?” The maidens replied, “Only two baskets of small peaches and three baskets of medium ones. At the back of the orchard, not even half a large peach remained. We believe the Great Sage must have stolen and eaten them all. While we were searching, the Great Sage unexpectedly came out, assaulted and threatened us, and demanded to know who had been invited to the banquet. We told him all about the previous banquet, whereupon he froze us in place and vanished to parts unknown. Only now have we regained our senses and been freed to return.”

p.src: On hearing this, the Queen Mother immediately went to see the Jade Emperor and related the whole affair. Before she had finished, the wine-makers and a company of immortal officials also came to report: “Someone unknown has thrown the Peach Banquet into disorder and stolen the jade liquor and nectar; all the eight delicacies and hundred flavors have been stolen and eaten as well.” Then the four Great Celestial Masters came to announce, “The Supreme Patriarch of the Way has arrived.” The Jade Emperor and the Queen Mother went out at once to receive him. When Laozi had completed his courtly salutations, he said, “This old Daoist refined a quantity of Ninefold-Cycled Golden Elixir in my palace, intending it for Your Majesty's Cinnabar Prime Banquet. Unexpectedly, a thief has stolen it, so I have come especially to inform Your Majesty.” The Jade Emperor was alarmed by this report. A short while later, an immortal clerk from the Office of the Great Sage Equal to Heaven kowtowed and reported, “Great Sage Sun has neglected his duties. He went out yesterday and has not yet returned, nor do we know where he has gone.” The Jade Emperor's suspicions deepened. Then the Barefoot Immortal bowed his head and reported, “By the Queen Mother's summons, your subject set out for the banquet yesterday. On the way I happened to meet the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, who told me that Your Majesty had issued a decree ordering him to invite us first to the Hall of Universal Radiance to rehearse the ceremonies, and only afterward attend the banquet. Taking him at his word, I turned back and went outside the Hall of Universal Radiance. When I saw neither Your Majesty's dragon carriage nor phoenix palanquin, I hurried here to await you.” The Jade Emperor was more startled than ever. “That scoundrel falsely proclaimed an imperial decree and deceived you, worthy minister. Order the Investigating Divine Officer to trace the scoundrel's whereabouts at once.”

p.src: The Divine Officer received the decree, left the hall, and investigated everywhere. Having learned all the details, he returned and reported, “The one who threw Heaven into disorder was none other than the Great Sage Equal to Heaven.” He then recounted the whole course of events. The Jade Emperor flew into a rage. He dispatched the Four Great Heavenly Kings, together with Heavenly King Li and Prince Nezha, and mustered the Twenty-Eight Lodges, the Officers of the Nine Luminaries, the Twelve Zodiac Gods, the Five Directional Guardians, the Four Duty Officers, the eastern and western constellations, the two gods of North and South, the gods of the Five Sacred Mountains and Four Great Rivers, and all the celestial constellations—one hundred thousand heavenly troops in all. They were to spread eighteen layers of celestial and terrestrial nets, descend to the lower world, surround Flower-Fruit Mountain, capture the scoundrel without fail, and punish him.

p.src: At that time Heavenly King Li gave his orders. The heavenly troops pitched camp and sealed Flower-Fruit Mountain so tightly that not even water could pass through. They spread eighteen layers of celestial and terrestrial nets above and below, then first sent the baleful Nine Luminaries into battle. The Nine Luminaries led their troops straight to the cave entrance, where they saw monkeys large and small leaping about at play. The star officers shouted fiercely, “You little fiends! Where is that Great Sage of yours? We are gods dispatched from the upper realm, come here to subdue your rebellious Great Sage. Tell him to come and surrender at once; if he utters so much as half a word of refusal, every one of you will be put to death.” The little fiends hurried inside in alarm and reported, “Great Sage, disaster! Disaster! Outside are nine fearsome gods who claim to have been sent from the upper realm to force you to surrender.”

p.src: The Great Sage was drinking immortal wine with the demon kings of the seventy-two caves and his four stalwart commanders. On hearing the report, he ignored it completely and said, “When there is wine today, get drunk today; never mind the rights and wrongs outside the gate.” Before he had finished speaking, another band of little fiends came leaping in and reported, “Those nine fearsome gods are hurling foul abuse and challenging us to battle outside the gate.” The Great Sage laughed. “Pay them no heed. With verse and wine, let us enjoy today; ask not when glory and achievement shall come.” He had scarcely finished when yet another group of little fiends came to report, “Master! Those nine fearsome gods have broken down the gate and are fighting their way in!” The Great Sage said angrily, “Those wretched petty gods are utterly insolent! I meant not to bother with them, yet how dare they come to my gate and bully me?” He immediately ordered the Single-Horned Demon King, “Lead the demon kings of the seventy-two caves into battle. Old Sun will follow with the four stalwart commanders.” The Demon King swiftly led the demon troops out to meet the enemy, but the baleful Nine Luminaries charged them all at once and pinned them at the Iron-Plank Bridge, leaving them unable to break through.

p.src: Amid the uproar, the Great Sage arrived and cried, “Make way!” He drew out his iron staff and gave it a shake. It grew as thick as a rice bowl and twenty-four feet long. Assuming his fighting stance, he battered his way out. None of the Nine Luminaries dared withstand him, and in moments they were beaten back. The Nine Luminaries steadied their battle line and cried, “You reckless Keeper of the Heavenly Stables, you have committed the ten abominable crimes! First you stole the peaches, then the wine, throwing the Peach Banquet into chaos. You also stole Laozi's immortal elixir and brought the imperial wine here for your own pleasure. You have piled crime upon crime—can you truly be unaware of it?” The Great Sage laughed. “Those charges are true, every one of them. But what do you intend to do about it now?” The Nine Luminaries replied, “By the Jade Emperor's golden decree, we have led these forces here to compel your surrender. Submit at once, so that these creatures need not lose their lives. Otherwise, we shall level this mountain and overturn this cave.” The Great Sage flew into a rage. “What powers could petty gods like you possess, that you dare utter such wild boasts? Do not run—come taste a blow from Old Sun's staff!” The Nine Luminaries all sprang forward together; but the Handsome Monkey King showed not the slightest fear. Brandishing his golden-hooped staff, he parried to left and right. He fought the Nine Luminaries until their muscles were exhausted and their limbs went weak. One after another, they fled in defeat, dragging their weapons behind them. Hurrying into the central commander's tent, they told Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li, “That Monkey King is truly an incomparable warrior. We could not defeat him and have returned in rout.”

p.src: With his single staff, the Great Sage held off the Four Great Heavenly Gods, Pagoda-Bearing Li, and Prince Nezha, all fighting high in midair for a long while. Seeing that evening was drawing near, the Great Sage plucked out a handful of hairs, tossed them into his mouth, chewed them to pieces, spat them out, and cried, “Transform!” At once they became hundreds upon hundreds of Great Sages, each wielding a golden-hooped staff. They drove back Prince Nezha and defeated all five heavenly kings.

p.src: Victorious, the Great Sage gathered back his hairs and hurriedly turned toward the cave. At the Iron-Plank Bridge he found the four valiant commanders leading the host in a kowtow of welcome. The whole company choked with sobs and wept aloud three times, then laughed merrily three times. The Great Sage said, “Why do you both weep and laugh when you see me?” The four valiant commanders said, “This morning, when you led the host into battle against the Heavenly Kings, all the demon kings of the seventy-two caves and the One-Horned Demon King were captured by the gods. We alone escaped with our lives, and therefore we had cause to weep. But now we see the Great Sage return victorious and unharmed, and therefore we have cause to laugh.” The Great Sage said, “Victory and defeat are both common in war. The ancients said, ‘Slay ten thousand men, and you will lose three thousand of your own.’ Besides, the chieftains they carried off were merely tigers, leopards, wolves, insects, badgers, deer, foxes, raccoon dogs, and the like. Not one of my own kind was harmed, so why should we grieve? Though I drove them back with my art of multiplying myself, they still intend to pitch camp at the foot of my mountain. For now, let us guard the mountain closely, eat our fill, sleep without worry, and restore our strength. At daybreak, watch me work a mighty wonder, capture those celestial generals, and avenge our comrades.” The four commanders and the other monkeys drank several bowls of coconut wine, then went peacefully to sleep. Of them we shall speak no more.

p.src: The Four Great Heavenly Kings recalled their troops and ended the fighting, and each contingent reported its achievements: some had captured tigers and leopards, some lions and elephants, and others wolves, insects, foxes, and raccoon dogs. Yet they had not captured a single monkey spirit. They then duly set their wagons in position and established a great encampment. The generals who had distinguished themselves were rewarded, and the troops forming the all-encompassing net of Heaven and Earth were ordered to patrol with bells and call out the watchwords. Thus they surrounded and blockaded the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, waiting only for the great battle on the following morning. Each man obeyed the order and guarded his assigned post with care. And so it was that:
